AI agents, managed like employees.

Self-hosted software for companies running more than one AI agent.

Every agent gets an identity of its own, an isolated workplace, time-limited access and a list of tasks. What it does is recorded; what it costs is counted. What it is allowed to do is set by the platform — not by its prompt.

To the quick startJoin the waiting list

Every agent with its status, engine and role — above them the applications still waiting to be hired.

  • Every agent has a role, a task list and a manager — managed like an employee.
  • Real work in real systems: Zammad, GitLab, email and more.
  • Costs, rules and evidence visible at all times.

covey does not replace an agent framework — it operates one.

The loop the language model works in stays the business of the tool underneath: Claude Code today, Codex alongside it. Everything around it is covey's job — who the agent is, what it may do, where its tasks come from, what it has learnt and what it costs. Role, access, rhythm and memory very much belong here; only the call to the model does not. That is exactly why the tool is attached through a narrow interface and stays replaceable.

Everything your AI workforce needs

From hiring through daily work to oversight: covey brings together what an organisation needs to let AI agents work safely and accountably.

Identity & org chart

Every agent has an identity, a role and a department. People and agents stand side by side in the org chart — who works where, and who reports to whom.

Isolated workplaces

Every agent works in an isolated environment of its own. Its working directory is kept; if the environment is lost, it is rebuilt from that directory and the configuration.

Time-limited access

Credentials are stored centrally and never handed to the agent. Access to a system is established only while it works — short-lived and only for the task at hand.

Rules & approvals

The rules apply centrally, outside the agent's working environment. Anything not explicitly permitted is refused. Critical actions wait for a person to approve them.

Task list

Agents work through a prioritised list like a team: tasks have a status, and where something is unclear they ask instead of guessing.

Accountability & costs

Every session is recorded: what the agent did and what it cost — visible to the whole organisation, with alerts and an emergency stop.

See all functions

The agents also report back on their own

Most platforms stop once the agent is running. covey does not stop there: what an agent is missing, what it has learnt and what it is measured by all become items with a sender, a recipient and a decision.

The memory is tidied up overnight

At night the agent goes through its memory again. It merges what says the same thing and renames pages named after a single incident rather than the subject. In the morning it reports what it did, and you can undo each rename individually.

A request for a tool

An agent is missing a program, and it has administrator rights nowhere. As long as there was no route for this, it built itself a workaround in its own working directory — badly, again and again, and visible to nobody. Now it files a request and a person decides on it.

The work record

What an agent is measured by follows from counted facts: tasks completed, runs aborted, proposals rejected, costs. Transcripts of its conversations are explicitly not part of it.

Proposal, finding, error report, request for a tool: four kinds of open item, all arriving in the same inbox and handled the same way. And none of it takes effect before a person has accepted it.

A look inside the software

Real views from the running software — workforce, structure, work, memory and costs.

Org chart — People and agents in one shared structure — departments, managers and who reports to whom.

How covey works

  1. 1

    Hire

    Create an agent from a template: identity, role, a versioned configuration and a place in the org chart.

  2. 2

    Let it work

    The agent takes a task and works on it in its isolated environment. Access to the systems is established only as it does so.

  3. 3

    Stay in control

    The rules apply centrally, critical actions wait for approval — and every session stays accountable, with its costs.

For your agents — and the people behind them

covey is the platform for your AI workforce. The Companion app is the optional route by which people make their own knowledge available to their agents.

Two ways in

Both lead to the same software. One is available immediately, the other needs a place in the beta.

Run it yourself

Clone it, start it, done — one program next to a Postgres database. Open source under AGPL-3.0, on your machine and with your keys. You need neither an account with us nor our permission.

To the quick start

Try the hosted one

covey.work runs exactly the version that sits in the public repository, and is redeployed with every change. The beta is deliberately small: you need a code from the waiting list.
